correctness.rationale: For all positive level sizes and the stated height restrictions, exact 3-pebble truncation and a complete three-round atomic-diagram invariant reduce the theorem to exhaustive finite comparisons: 3279 distinct signatures up to seven levels, 6417 signatures from 6561 eight-level tuples, exactly 144 two-element fibers with the stated boundary pattern. Stabilizer-orbit enumeration agrees on all 3279; an independent two-sided game agrees on positive and negative instances. Independent audit is not claimed.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2010 Mwesigye–Truss original classification concerns unary-coloured linear orders and gives generic recursion and small-depth bounds, not this pure strict-order weak-order finite census. Its follow-up (2018 online) builds examples for coloured words; neither states the 3279 up-to-seven classification, 6417 exactly-eight classification, or 144 central swaps. Accessible prior records and actual semantic queries identified no statement implying this theorem; the languages and invariants differ. Residual index incompleteness is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Index and full-text retrieval may miss an equivalent weak-order formulation.

value.rationale: Weak-order tie classes are canonical in finite preference orderings. The result identifies a sharp boundary where shallow FO ceases to recover every ordered capped tie size, and completely classifies the first new degeneracy by an explicit 144-pair central-swap law, rather than presenting arbitrary small cases or a mere known finite-order cutoff.
